The wait is bounded and the call returns either an outcome or "still
running" — it never holds a connection open for the work's lifetime, which
is what drops under load and leaves a caller unable to tell a dead stream
from a dead job. A job whose supervisor died reads back as unknown with
timedOut false, its own third case distinct from both success and "still
running" — never re-await it expecting a different answer.

The reported job's aliveAgeMs is the faster of the two signals: it crosses
the 5000ms caller threshold before state necessarily catches up, so a
caller in a hurry can act on it directly instead of waiting for the next
reconcile (see `erun exec job status --help`).

--timeout is capped at 10m: a wait bounded well past the length of a single
call is the same held-connection failure mode this command exists to avoid,
just at a larger size. A job that runs longer than 10m (the full test suite
gate routinely does) is not a case this command refuses to cover -- call it
again each time it reports the job still running (exit 124) rather than
asking for a single longer wait; a timeout past the cap is refused outright,
naming the 10m ceiling in the refusal.

Exit codes are the contract: 0 when the job exited 0, 124 when the timeout
elapsed with the job still running, 125 when the outcome is unknown, and 1
when the job exited non-zero (its real code is in the reported result). 124
is never a verdict on the job -- it means only that this one call's own
bounded wait elapsed, and the documented response is to call await again,
not to treat the silence as an answer.

Usage:
  erun job await [flags]

Examples:
  erun exec job await --tenant team --environment dev --id suite --timeout 2m

  # A gate that can run longer than the 10m ceiling: keep awaiting at the
  # ceiling until it stops reporting 124.
  erun exec job await --tenant team --environment dev --id suite --timeout 10m

Flags:
      --dry-run              Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
      --environment string   Environment the job runs in
  -h, --help                 help for await
      --id string            Job to wait for
      --tenant string        Tenant whose environment the job belongs to
      --timeout duration     How long to wait before reporting the job as still running (capped at 10m0s; call await again to keep waiting past it) (default 30s)

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
